results.title: SavorApp_AI: Capture what matters and move your intentions forward | Product Hunt
results.content:
SAVOR is built around a problem we don't think AI assistants have really solved. AI assistants are increasingly good at executing clearly defined tasks and goals. But those tasks and goals flow from the intentions that motivate them, something profoundly human. Two people can pursue exactly the same goal, but the right actions, tradeoffs, and outcomes can vary dramatically depending on why they're pursuing it. And any single intention is best understood in the context of all the other things that matter to that person.

We're not trying to build another chatbot or general-purpose assistant. We're building what we call an Intention Layer™—a system that captures what matters to you, gives it structure, holds onto it over time, resurfaces it when relevant, and helps you move toward action. [...] They’re half-formed intentions—something we want to look into, a decision we need to make, someone we mean to reach out to, an idea we don’t want to lose, a change we’d like to make. Most productivity systems ask us to turn all of that into lists and projects, and eventually the system itself becomes another thing to manage.

We wanted something different: a calm place where you can simply say what’s on your mind, trust that it won’t disappear, and have it come back when it can actually help you move forward.

That’s SAVOR today. [...] We believe a person's most valuable resources are their time, attention, presence, and focus. And we want sAVoR to be a tool that helps them cultivate those things and direct them to the arenas where they want them. One user might get a lot of satisfaction from getting through a lot of tasks, but another user may view their tasks as endless and want to just prioritize the ones they find essential (so that they can spend more time on their passion: swimming or crocheting or whatever it is).

A lot of productivity apps are designed to encourage more engagement, more activity, and more boxes checked. But we don't believe that being more productive necessarily means living a better or more fulfilling life. Sometimes the most valuable thing you can do is absolutely nothing on your to-do list.
